The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Zarak half-sister to winners, chief among them Calandagan, and won two of her three starts over 1m4f, the most recent a Listed success from Romantic Symphony a couple of months ago on good ground, with the defeat coming behind Dispatches; holds Group 1 entries and capable of more improvement.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Improved this season upped in trip, winning on her handicap debut at Ascot and picking up a 1m2f soft-ground Listed race on soft at Goodwood in June when cheekpieces were first tried; 50-1 and well beaten in the Ribblesdale Stakes (1m4f, good to firm) but may don better off a break and down in grade; likes to go from the front.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Won twice as a 2yo and gone close in Listed, Group 2 and Group 1 company this campaign, her most recent run seeing her 3.25l fourth in the Prix de Diane (1m2f110yds, good to firm); anything like that sort of form on her first try at this trip (some stamina in her pedigree) would see her a leading player for this.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Solid performer this season and not beaten far by some classy types following a couple of wins at the start of the year; close to her best in a 1m2f soft-ground Listed race at Vichy just over three weeks ago, and a good effort couldn't be ruled out.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: From a good family and only modest effort came when when favourite for Lingfield Oaks Trial in the spring, but in decent form either side of that, following a second to Calasita in a Listed event (1m4f, good) in June with a Listed win at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) two weeks ago; stable in form.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Won three is a row, which included beating Calasita a length at Compiegne in May in a conditions race; hat-trick was landed in a Listed event at Longchamp (1m2f, good to soft) before being beaten by a top prospect at the same track in a Group 2 on first try over 1m4f; likely to be involved.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Kept some good company since winning here on the AW in November but has finished behind Dispatches the last two times they've met, including over this trip, so work to do with that rival.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: 3-15 on AW (last two wins were at this track) compared to 0-4 on turf; in good form at 1m4f on AW initially this year, including a second under Taryn Langley; there was a dip in April when last seen but it's easy to see him returning in a major role for his in-form yard.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: Fourth in the German 2,000 Guineas (1m, good) in May 2025 on his third start; however, absent for a year afterwards and he's been way below that form in his three starts for new yard this year, tenth of 11 on handicap debut last time; goes beyond 1m for the first time and, although he's by a speed influence, his dam was a good 1m-12.5f winner.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: Two wins this year over 1m4f on Lingfield Polytrack, dictating the pace on second occasion; good third at Kempton (also 1m4f on Polytrack) on latest start, which gives him each-way claims if it's transferred to Tapeta.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: Dam 1m3f winner; 1m, heavy-ground maiden winner last September for Paddy Twomey; after his four 1m/1m2f handicaps for current yard this term, trying cheekpieces last time, others bring much more persuasive claims.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: Won two handicaps over about 1m4f last summer, in a mixed record; one of the lesser efforts was his AW debut (Kempton Polytrack) when last seen; left Richard Hannon for 20,000gns last October and this is his first run since (gelded in interim).

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: 50-1 winner of this race last year off 4lb lower; following 228 days off; 10l winner over hurdles this March, followed by two modest shows in May; had wind operation (his second) in July and needs a second look.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: Won off this mark over C&D last November; that's her only win from nine races and she was well beaten when 28-1 under 7lb claimer at Newcastle (Tapeta) last time, but her stable is in good form.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: Has the same mark as when winning at Lingfield (1m1f, good to firm) almost exactly one year ago, on her final start last season and the last time she was ridden by Billy Loughnane; that was her fifth career win, and she stays 1m4f and used to look effective on Tapeta but a revival is needed on this first run since May.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: Back to some form over 1m4f on turf on last two starts; 0-11 on AW, however, with two places but they were on Polytrack.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: 2-4 for this yard with narrow wins at Ripon (1m) and Doncaster (1m2f); another creditable effort over 1m2f last time; needs to resume improvement, which may be possible as he's just a 3yo but he's not bred for this new trip; it's also his AW debut.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: Won a 9.4f maiden at Wolverhampton (Tapeta) in April and over 11.4f on turf at Windsor in June in his second handicap; that's two wins from four starts and that latest performance was encouraging for this second crack at 1m4f; 3yo to consider seriously.

RaceName: Newark Advertiser Handicap (GBBPus Race)
Spotlight: Best novice effort when fourth over 1m2f at Nottingham on second start, making most; never-dangerous ninth of 14 when 16-1 for handicap debut here six weeks ago but that was over just 1m, whereas his dam was a useful bumper and 1m6f Flat winner; stepped up markedly to 1m4f, he could now be a great deal more interesting.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Only made debut in late June and not made much progress yet, although was beaten under a length over C&D a week ago; hard task to get first win in this race.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Won well on debut at York's Dante meeting (5f, good) and then went on to be fourth in the Coventry at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm); not so good in the Richmond Stakes after but can forgive a modest effort at Goodwood; enough in pedigree to suggest 7f won't be a problem if bouncing back.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Supplemented for this; holds Group 1 entries and made a winning debut at Doncaster just over three weeks ago (7f, good to firm) from a colt who won next time; could be anything.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Debut winner at Newbury (6.5f, good to soft) before a step up in form to be fourth in a Group 2 at Newmarket (7f, good to firm); didn't build on that dropped into Listed company after but beginning to shape like a solid performer and should be thereabouts.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Won on debut by 4l at this trip on soft ground and then picked up a Listed event here over 7f on the Round Course from the front when last seen a month and a half ago; that form looks solid and he might be hard to pass.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
Spotlight: Reacted well to the addition of cheekpieces when a narrow winner from Seven Nation Army in a C&D nursery; raised 7lb and was almost 2l behind Battle Of The Boyne when fourth in the Galway race won by Seven Nation Army; blinkered this time.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
Spotlight: Showed little on his first two starts; was able to dictate in a 6f Fairyhouse maiden and gave a much-improved display to take second; no match for a Joseph O'Brien-trained winner at Galway (I Ready back in fourth); might not cope with Mr Montauk now.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
Spotlight: Ordinary form in maidens at Listowel and Down Royal; stepped up considerably on those runs to win at Navan on a superb day for her trainer; sights are lowered considerably now following a Listed bid at Naas.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
Spotlight: Failed to run to expectations when favourite for a C&D maiden on debut; best of his three outings was over 1m at Bellewstown; this trip may prove inadequate.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
Spotlight: All four runs over 5f; best display on debut when second to the smart Velozee (third in last Sunday's Phoenix Stakes) on soft ground at Cork; subsequent form on good going raises doubts.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
Spotlight: Failed to run to market expectations when favourite on debut at Cork (5f, soft); better effort at Navan (5f, good) when fourth of nine; struggled in a conditions race last time; stable also represented by Oisin Murphy's mount Alrashdeyah.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
Spotlight: Long odds for first two starts and soundly beaten; Bellewstown fourth was a step in the right direction; others have more convincing claims

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
Spotlight: Oisin Murphy booked; hard to take positives from her maiden form; very poor at Bellewstown when last of eight; hood used then is now discarded.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)
Spotlight: Three qualifying runs over 5f, all within the space of three weeks in April/May; sent off second-favourite for a 5f Down Royal nursery last month, got outpaced and then hampered at a crucial stage when staying on; chased home a strongly fancied rival from the Paddy Twomey stable at Sligo, good chance he can go one better.

RaceName: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Fair sort on the Flat, winning 1m7f Leopardstown handicap last summer, albeit latest two efforts have been well below his best; 0-6 hurdling, narrowly beaten in C&D maiden at this meeting last year his best effort; chance if returning to that sort of form.

RaceName: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Not the force of old (one-time useful AW handicapper) but runner-up in modest maiden hurdle company in Britain this summer at Stratford (twice) and after making most (carrying head awkwardly, hung right) at Worcester (2m, good); no show on handicap debut at Galway and back into maiden company probably with a bit to find.

RaceName: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Won on the Flat in France last year (1m2f, soft) and had Listowel maiden hurdle (2m4f, good to yielding) at his mercy before last-flight fall on stable debut in May; clear second to an odds-on shot at Cartmel last month (2m1f), having been clear for much of the way; hood now fitted and likely the one to beat.

RaceName: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Nathaniel half-brother to four winners, notably useful bumper and hurdles performer Mongibello; dam French 1m1f/10.5f winner, half-sister to French 2m5f Grade 3 hurdle winner; beaten favourite but showed some promise on debut in Ballinrobe bumper last month; quickly switches to hurdles.

RaceName: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Very lightly raced in Britain, initially with Alan King and then in two runs at Stratford for Jamie Snowdon, latter occasion when last in 2m maiden hurdle in May 2024; tongue-tied on debut for Andy Slattery and watching brief advised.

RaceName: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Runner-up in maiden hurdles at Clonmel (2m4f) in May and Punchestown (3m) in June; not so good the last twice back in trip and has it to do here.

RaceName: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Soundly beaten on debut in Kilbeggan bumper and none too fluent on hurdles debut at Killarney last month; can only be watched for now.

RaceName: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Some promise in Flat maidens last year but has been disappointing in handicaps this term; hurdles debut was a bit more encouraging when third in 2m2f Sligo maiden, despite some novicey jumping, but didn't improve at Kilbeggan; drops in trip here.

RaceName: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Ghaiyyath 4yo ran to a useful level of form on the Flat last year for Charlie Fellows at around 1m4f; yard debut effort at Galway was respectable, considering he was plenty fresh; interesting now switched to hurdles and one to consider.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: Second in two novice/maiden events last year but she's failed to beat a rival in any of her last four starts, including three handicaps this year.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: No claims from last two starts but he was a C&D winner last December and second over C&D this April, which give him a chance.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: The last four of his five wins were over 1m on Newcastle Tapeta (hampered on sole start here); looked an unlucky loser at Newcastle on penultimate start but bled from the nose when a disappointing favourite there on latest; player if straight back to form.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: Benefited from the drop into 0-50 classified company when off the mark at the 14th attempt at Lingfield (1m, Polytrack) five weeks ago; more is needed on this return to a handicap and she has more to prove on Tapeta.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: Yet to make the first three after 11 races from 6f to 1m2f; 18lb lower now than on last summer's handicap debut but others are more solid.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: Both AW wins (his latest) were on Kempton Polytrack in November 2024; effective over C&D, edging down the weights and often not far away but others are preferred for win purposes.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
OwnerName: Dixon, Wylam, M Baldry, J&s Harrod
Spotlight: Three C&D wins; competitive only twice in 2026 but latest instance saw her register a turf win at Ffos Las (1m) 19 days ago; player if backing that up.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: First 27 starts came on the AW with three wins, including two over C&D last October; rather patchy this year but he was third of 13 when making his turf debut at Doncaster (7f) in May and probably not discredited in a two-runner turf race in June when last seen; in the mix.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: Accomplished little in three novices, though he did attract the stewards' attention on third start; weakened into ninth of 13 when 22-1 for handicap debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f) on latest outing; all four were on Tapeta; down 2lb but no solid form.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: C&D winner in 2024 and scored at Wolverhampton last October; finished last season on a downswing and well beaten at 40-1 for reappearance two months ago, which he might have needed but absent again since; market may guide.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: Low-level form in all five starts, including one handicap (C&D last October); he was triple-figure odds for all of them, so the market has been a pretty good guide so far; seasonal debut.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: 0-18 but second in three of his last four starts; made most on last two occasions, the latest over 7f on Newcastle Tapeta; there's a bit more for him to prove at this track and over 1m.

RaceName: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap
Spotlight: 4-29 record includes a Nottingham win (1m) in April on reappearance but he's been out of form in recent outings; now makes his AW debut.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Showed strong potential for success in a race like this with a debut second in a 17-runner contest at Navan; winner Shesthedevil will put that form to the test in the opening nursery.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: First outing at Leopardstown was more encouraging than Wednesday's mid-division Gowran effort; more likely a handicap prospect.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: GBP58,000 Y; first foal; dam 7f winner, half-sister to several winners; speedy pedigree, could go well on debut.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Has finished in front of only one of his 27 rivals in races at Naas and Sligo.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Naas run represented an improvement from his debut at Navan, a lot more progress needed.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Ran green but showed some ability when 5l seventh of 12 on his debut at Leopardstown; improvement is feasible.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Ninth foal; Kodi Bear filly is a sister to 6f turf Listed/7f AW winner Clounmacon, half-sister to three other winners, including the versatile Nibiru; dam 6f winner, including at two; of some interest.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Invincible Army colt has a decent pedigree, from the immediate family of 6f Group 1 winner G Force and US 1m Grade 3 winner Louvain (dam of French 1,000 Guineas winner Flotilla); failed to sell cheaply as a yearling.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Tailed off when the rank outsider of five at Leopardstown last month; can be ruled out.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Medallion Racing 2020 LLC/B Fowler/Reeves T'bred/ S I Weston
Spotlight: E25,000 yearling, cost 200,000gns at Tatts Craven Breeze-Up in April; by Ten Sovereigns filly; dam 6f AW 2yo winner, out of Listed-placed middle-distance winner by Oasis Dream.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Cheap yearling; half-sister by Lucky Vega to a 1m winner; dam a US-Stakes winner from a solid family; plenty of speed in trhe pedigree.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Ran respectably first time out in a 7f maiden at Galway; open to improvement; hard to be sure if drop to 6f will be a help or a hindrance.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: First foal; Alkumait colt, dam 5f winner by Ardan, half-sister to 6f 2yo winner Nifty; others are more likely.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Finished behind Heart Of You at Galway on the more recent of two outings; might need to qualify for a handicap mark.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Plenty of improvement is needed from her opening efforts at Naas and Cork.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Second foal. half-sister by Earthlight to an AW winner; dam a winning daughter of Iffraaj.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Made late headway from an unpromising position at Bellewstown; well beaten at Leopardstown.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Fifth foal; Arizona filly, closely related to three winners by No Nay Never; unraced dam out of US 1m winning half-sister to 6f/7f Group 1 winner Wolfhound and to smart dam of BC Classic winner A P Indy; cheekpieces on for debut

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Conor O'Connor & Colum Currie & Mark Devenny
Spotlight: Won as a 2yo on the Flat; some decent efforts in defeat mixing both codes lately but needs to find more on this second handicap hurdle start.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Showed glimpses of promise in maidens but has been poor in two handicap starts; can't be ruled out from this top yard but a tongue-tie will have to make a significant difference.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: A wide-margin Flat winner here in 2025 got off the mark over hurdles on return at Cork last time, still showing greenness; a 13lb hike is plenty but has to be considered with more to come.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has been badly regressive over hurdles this year and was withdrawn on the Flat recently after being unruly before the start; not easy to fancy.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: The best of four maiden hurdle runs came at Kilbeggan last time; can do better now in handicaps and local yard targets this meeting so is worth checking the market.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Maiden under both codes has been running well enough in defeat lately but he has run poorly both starts at this course so questions in that respect.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Ed Mulligan & John Finnegan & Aileen Saunders & Ann Holton
Spotlight: A heavy ground chase winner last winter ran one of his best hurdle races at this track in 2024; not a bad run in a claimer last time and could go well.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Second runner for yard; some promise in points; modest in maiden hurdles but travelled strongly before weakening over 2m5f on handicap debut here three days ago; this trip can suite better, notable jockey booking so one to consider.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Well beaten in a bumper and four maiden hurdles but should do better now in handicaps.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Sole hurdle win came in 2022; not many runs since and fell early at Cork last time; isn't high on the list.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Maiden in all spheres has been placed a few times but is coming back from a layoff so others are preferred.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Sole win came in this race last year off the same mark; not bad efforts at Cork and Kilbeggan lately so has to enter calculations back at this venue.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Maiden has run well enough last two starts with blinkers added but has to find more down 1lb.

RaceName: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Showed little in maidens and was pulled-up on handicap debut at Listowel last year so not easy to fancy.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: 750,000gns yearling by Lope De Vega; 6-5 for his debut in a 12-runner maiden at Kempton (1m, AW) in January and came from midfield to stride clear; the next two in that race have done well since; off 200 days but one of the two leading contenders on form and probably an exciting prospect.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: 16-1 and 200-1 when behind at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) and Wolverhampton (7f, AW) this summer.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: Remote when 500-1 at Beverley (7.4f, good) in June, blowing the start.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: 700,000gns yearling by Frankel; dam 5f/6f winner (including Listed; RPR 109); rather slowly into his stride on his way to a 20l defeat in novice at Salisbury (6f, good to firm) last July; presumably showed a lot more at home prior to that, as he started 5-4 favourite, and it will be interesting to see if his backers go in again on this belated return.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: Fair form when fourth at Thirsk (7f, good) and Carlisle (7f, soft) this spring, with the latter suggesting that 1m would help; however, much better is needed if he's to overturn today's form principals.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: 66-1, always behind in novice at Newcastle (7f, AW) in June; has an extra 1f today but is bred for markedly further.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: Third foal; Night Of Thunder half-brother to winners Theory Of Tides (1m2f/11.4f; RPR 100) and Regalian (7f AW; 90); dam Australian 5f/6f winner (including 2yo Group 3; 108), sister to Australian 5f Group 2 winner; needs a check but probably finds himself in a warm race for debut.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: 9-2, very green early on in a novice at Nottingham (1m, good to firm) 17 days ago and left himself with a lot to do, unable to pass any of his four rivals; should do better but no claims yet.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: 50-1 second of 13 in C&D novice in June, always prominent, but his fourth of six at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) three weeks later was well below that form; a major contender if reverting to his debut form and his sire was a US dirt performer, so the return to AW may well suit.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: Low-level form when 150-1 and slowly away at Leicester (1m, good) and Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW), so he looks one for handicaps in due course.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: 6f winner last year; never involved on seasonal return at Naas in May; met trouble in running at Gowran nine days ago, when Neo Smart finished three places ahead of her; contender now.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Two wins on AW, 1-30 turf record is a negative; respectable form lately; not a lost cause judged on her fourth in a 20-runner C&D event and same placing at Gowran nine days ago.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
OwnerName: Charles Kerwin & Brendan Kerwin & Liam Kehoe
Spotlight: Three wins this year; unplaced in four outings since a Roscommon victory in May; needs to show signs of a return to form before being a betting proposition again.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Recorded her sole success in this race last season; also ran well when third in a 26-runner contest here late last season; uneven form this term; stable has hit a good patch of form this week; worth considering.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Fair AW form late last year; 40-1 and ran accordingly on handicap/turf/seasonal debut at Killarney last month.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: A winner of seven races on AW and three on turf; last turf success was in 2022, but this season's overall form provided a fair amount of encouragement; a three-time runner-up at this venue, including in June; had plenty of horses behind him at Leopardstown ten days ago.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Placed only once from 13 starts, may have needed a recent run after a break; not the most consistent type.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Ran respectably in three decent maidens over a mile last year; should be better for her handicap/seasonal debut over 7f at Naas; this extra furlong should suit.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Moderate form in her three handicap outings; hard to identify her optimum distance; others are more appealing.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Took a long time to win a race; scored twice last season and added another win last month in first-time cheekpieces, overcoming a slow start to score over this trip at Naas; had a troubled passage and found 7f a bit sharp at Galway.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Ordinary form in maidens; stayed on for third over this trip at Cork in June on his handicap debut; failed to stay the extended 1m2f in a recent Sligo claimer.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Placed in all but one of her five handicap starts; capable of winning one with just a little improvement; the addition of cheekpieces could perhaps make the difference.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Winner this year over 1m at Dundalk and 1m2f at Fairyhouse in June; good form in defeat over 1m1f at Leopardstown, beaten a neck in a 22-runner contest; fair run over a longer trip last time, this may be closer to his best distance.

RaceName: Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap
Spotlight: Failed to beat a single opponent in her first three races this term; attracted some support and produced a vastly improved effort at Leopardstown; possibly on the upgrade but 3lb wrong here; cheekpieces worn at Leopardstown are left off.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Unraced at two but created a fine impression last year, winning all four starts, including a convincing defeat of subsequent Group 1 winner Opera Ballo in the Joel Stakes; yet to match that form but not far off best when winning Group 2 at Ascot last time (better placed than More Thunder in a steadily run race); big chance back up in grade.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Group 3 winner at this venue nearly a year ago and better than ever judged on reappearance win at that level at Saint-Cloud in spring; not seen since but, although he handles a sound surface, his two best efforts (by some way) have both been on ground described as soft.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Has a good strike-rate and turned in best effort when bagging first Grade 1 over this trip on fast ground at Tokyo in June; not far behind the pick of the Europeans on that evidence and could be overpriced.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Did well to win - given he took a strong hold - a valuable Listed event at Abu Dhabi in February (July Cup wiinner Comanche Brave in third, Group 2 scorer Quddwah in fourth); long way below that level at Sha Tin last time and needs to return to his best.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Group 2 winner at Newbury last summer who posted solid efforts in Group 1 company on next three starts; failed to confirm Queen Anne placings with Zeus Olympios in steadily run Summer Mile at Ascot last time and he'll likely go well, especially if the gallop is honest.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Prolific winner with a fine strike-rate on AW and not far off pick of that form when beating subsequent dual winner Seagulls Eleven over this trip on a sound surface at Saint-Cloud in May; disappointed when last behind Zeus Olympios on most recent start and he has something to prove at this level.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Improved performer this year and registered first Group win when making all at Baden-Baden in June; hasn't been seen since and will find it harder to dominate in this company.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: 3-5 and turned in a clear pb to win the French 2,000 Guineas in May; failed to match that over 7f on quick ground behind Thesecretadversary in the Jean Prat but that proved his effectiveness on a sound surface and the form was franked when stable companion Samangan won the Maurice de Gheest; interesting back at 1m.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
OwnerName: Cayton Park Stud & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Held in both the English/Irish 2,000 Guineas and best form has been around 7f but does stay this trip and has shown improved form to win the Jersey and Group 1 Jean Prat on last two starts; may find one or two too strong back over this trip, though.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Disappointed in the 1,000 Guineas but bounced back to win the Irish equivalent and followed up in the Coronation Stakes; creditable second to Blue Bolt in both the Falmouth and Rothschild; tends to lose ground at the start but likely to go well getting the fillies' allowance on this first run against the boys.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Runner-up on sole point start before winning a 2m bumper at this meeting last year on second rules start; was poor in soft ground in a Listed bumper on sole 2026 run but has to be respected back here on hurdles debut on good ground; penalised 8lb, though.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Ran well enough before falling in a 3m Punchestown maiden hurdle two starts ago but was well beaten at Cork since; others preferred.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Ran well at times in bumpers without winning, including here; some solid efforts in four maiden hurdles but has fallen once and didn't jump that well last time so needs to do better.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Runner-up in a Cork maiden hurdle last November but no sign of that form in three runs since; the tongue-tie will have to make a major difference.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Has posted several solid efforts in defeat over hurdles, with best form coming at Clonmel; however, was pulled-up in a tongue-tie at Killarney last time but that is left off today so can rebound.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Has shown some ability in bumpers and maiden hurdles but has been pulled-up in two points this year; has to return to best for a new yard with cheekpieces added.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Modest form in bumpers and three maiden hurdles so handicaps will suit better after today.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Second runner for yard; didn't progress in seven points and well beaten at Cork on hurdling debut so best watched today.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Solid efforts in bumpers at Listowel and Wexford last autumn, beaten a head on latter occasion, both over 2m; is likely to be well prepared for this return and has the stamina in her pedigree for this trip; a major player.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Well beaten in a Killarney bumper on debut and can only be watched for the time being.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Finished third over hurdles in Ireland; beaten a shade under 10l in two 8.6f non-handicaps at Wolverhampton for this yard; very vulnerable.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Half-sister to the yard's smart Native Warrior; odds-on when defying greenness at Ripon 20 days ago (1m) and that was promising, for all that the second has since extended her losing streak to six; clear claims with improvement on the cards.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: She wasn't far away in a C&D maiden on second run in April 2025 on what proved her final race for Karl Burke; left that yard for 2,000gns.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Night Of Thunder newcomer out of a Frankel mare who won over 1m2f on the AW (RPR 95); has been gelded but he cost 260,000gns as a yearling and is of obvious interest, all the more so if strong in the betting.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Also tongue tied at Windsor (1m) where he was slowly away and always in rear; went off 33-1; no appeal after that.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Out the back early before staying on to some effect when fourth of nine over 6f here in April; there's some ability lurking but he'd be a surprise winner of this.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: 220,000gns yearling but didn't last long with Karl Burke, for whom he was tailed off in his only run over 6f at Newbury; gelded since changing hands for 5,000gns; can only be watched.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Showed a consistent level of form in four defeats (6f-7f) for Aidan O'Brien, whom he left for 24,000gns; has definite form claims but he's undergone wind surgery, sports new headgear (tried blinkers on second run) and has been off since October; market confidence would be welcomed.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: 300-1 when beaten 25l over 7f here last month.

RaceName: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Down the field in one run over 6f for Ed Walker and tailed off over Nottingham's 1m on recent yard debut.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: E420,000 F; eleventh foal; half-brother by Camelot to seven winners, including 1,000 Guineas winner Mother Earth and Pattern scorers Ocean Jewel and Night Colours; dam a Listed winner by Green Desert; one of three runners for the stable, good apprentice aboard.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: E120,000 Breeze Up purchase; already looked in need of further when a remote fourth over 7f at this venue on debut; likely to be capable of improvement from the experience gained then.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: E140,000 yearling; fourth foal; half-brother by Saxon Warrior to three winners who stayed middle distances effectively; dam Listed-placed winner on the Flat and useful 2m hurdle winner, sister to German 1m3f Group 3 winner Pagera.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: E65,000 Y; seventh foal; Sea The Stars colt is brother to five winners; dam AW winner, sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Buratino.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: E105,000 yearling; second foal; dam French 1m AW 2yo/1m1f turf winner, half-sister to French winners Likala (1m2f Listed) and Liyann (useful 1m 2yo), out of 1m 2yo winning half-sister to Australian 1m Group 2 winner Lidari.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Fourth foal; brother to US 8.5f turf winner Totally Justified, half-brother to two winners, including Masteroffoxhounds (US turf Grade 2; 115); dam 1m and 1m2f (Listed) winner, by Galileo, sister to BC Turf winner Magician.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: E42,000 yearling; tenth foal; half-brother by Dawn Approach to five winners including Group 2 scorer Turret Rocks (May Hill Stakes), and Beyond Thankful (Australian Group 3); dam placed 1m4f AW, out of well-related 1m2f winner.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: E300,000 yearling was the stable's second-string when third of four at Galway; finished 4l behind Zarak Pasha; may be capable of narrowing that gap with experience under his belt; from the Galileo/Sea The Stars family, so the extra distance can only help.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: Fifth foal; half-brother to US 1m turf winner For The Flag; dam runner-up 1m in France and US, sister to winners Civil Union (US 1m2f Grade 1) and War Dispatch (French 1m1f Group 3), out of unraced half-sister to HK 1m4f Group 1 winner Line Of Battle.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: A 75,000gns breeze-up purchase in April and from a middle-distance family; recovered from a slow start to run well over 1m on debut at Killarney; picked up useful experience behind an Aidan O'Brien-trained favourite at Galway and had 4l to spare over today's rival Thomas Chippendale; the selected of a stable quartet.

RaceName: Velo "Official Coffee At The Curragh" Irish EBF Maiden
OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Eighth foal; Camelot filly is a sister to middle-distance winner Sir Lamorak, half-sister to winners A New Dawn (Group-placed 6f 2yo) and Jewelry (6f 2yo); dam 5f 2yo winner, half-sister to 1m4f Group 1 winner Bracelet.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Dual point winner won a Clonmel maiden hurdle over 2m4f last autumn; posted some fine runs in defeat after in Listed and Grade 3 company; has to be respected on chasing debut even after a break.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Course winner over hurdles has been running well enough in that sphere lately; some decent efforts amongst her eight chase runs and needs to be at her best returned to this discipline.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Point winner is a maiden over hurdles and rated only 86 in that sphere so has a lot to find on chasing debut.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: One of three runners for yard; point, bumper and maiden hurdle winner fell on chasing debut at this venue but has been runner-up twice since at Wexford over 2m and 2m3f; just in front of stablemate La Note Verte last time; a big player if staying this trip.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Second runner for yard; dual hurdle winner is rated 123 in that sphere; fine efforts in both chase starts including when just behind stablemate Future Prospect at Wexford last time; her previous Killarney run was over 2m5f so this trip should be fine; big player.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Maiden is rated only 77 over hurdles so can't be fancied in this company on chasing debut.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Bumper and dual hurdle winner is rated 121 in that sphere though disappointed when last seen in 2025; makes chasing debut for a new yard and is respected but ran poorly on her only run at this track last year.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Third runner for yard; point and bumper winner hit form over hurdles last year, winning twice and getting to a rating of 127; seems to be the stable third string on return/chasing debut but can still give a good account.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Has some flashes of smart form (including on sole AW start when second to Notable Speech) so it's disappointing that he's won just once in ten races, and more new headgear was tried when sixth on his reappearance in the Lincoln; that was a pretty good effort from off the pace and he returns from another break after wind surgery and with no aids fitted; has a fair record when fresh, so dangerous to dismiss.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: A sixth win here when beating five rivals in March on latest outing (7f); went up only 2lb but lacking a recent run is probably not ideal in this much deeper race.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Won two turf novices as a 2yo, beating Wokingham winner Double Rush in the first; well below that level when confined to only two starts at Meydan in 2025 (both in January; one on AW); lots to prove on a few counts on handicap debut and with a tongue-tie tried, though any confidence behind him would turn some heads.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Won a 7f Tapeta maiden for the Crisfords and doubled his tally on third and final run for William Haggas when winning by 11l on soft ground at Ffos Las in June (first-time cheekpieces worn then are now removed); wouldn't want to be flattered by that having gone up 12lb; joined current connections last month for 30,000gns.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Won twice on turf in Ireland and had competitive form in a handicap at this trip; latest run there in a new tongue-tie was highly respectable and he could be interesting on yard debut with Billy Loughnane booked; AW debut.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Won at Redcar (1m) in April on yard debut but has beaten just one rival in two outings since; cheekpieces are quickly swapped for blinkers; has something to prove all of a sudden but the ability is lurking to take a hand.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: First six runs were at 1m and he had been disappointing in handicaps; however, that changed when dropped to 7f at Kempton last September and he's well handicapped on that comfortable 2l win despite this 8lb higher mark; it's encouraging that he returns from his absence with the yard in great form.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: 2-3 on AW surfaces; he's on a handy mark on last season's best efforts and the signs were more encouraging at Thirsk 15 days ago (7f), as although only midfield he wasn't beaten all that far; others are still preferred.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Impressed with two C&D wins during the winter and could leave subsequent struggles behind back on this surface; shouldn't be handicapped out of it.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Contested last year's Group 3 Acomb in between wins over 7f (one at Wolverhampton); still lightly raced and denied only late on last time at Chester (7f) where he appeared to have that in the bag when kicking clear after disputing the lead throughout; that effort is worthy of an upgrade; interesting.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Won once in Ireland and three times for George Boughey, twice on the AW and in a 7f Epsom handicap on final start for that yard; later sold for 28,000gns; had always worn a hood (also effective in tongue-tie) but went in blinkers on stable debut at Goodwood recently and raced too freely up front; now goes in an eyeshield; bit risky.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Three-time winner but now on a lengthy losing run and connections reverted to blinkers last time at Goodwood; needs to turn a corner.

RaceName: Coopers Marquees Handicap
Spotlight: Took strike-rate to 5-16 when winning comfortably at Chepstow (7f, good to soft) ten weeks ago, looking better than ever; 7lb higher in this classier contest but has run well here before and he's not easily knocked.

RaceName: Enter ITV7 For Free EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 40,000euros yearling, 85,000euros 2yo breeze-ups; fifth foal; Harry Angel half-brother to French winners Victoire Magique (1m2f/1m7f including 2yo/Listed) and Enchantment (1m1f AW); dam 1m-1m6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 98); makes debut with trainer's 2yos in good form; in calculations.

RaceName: Enter ITV7 For Free EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Second foal; dam 7f/1m winner (RPR 78), half-sister to winners Bocking End (1m-1m2f) and Archie Stevens (5f/6f including 2yo); a market check is advised but this Belardo newcomer is likely to improve for the outing.

RaceName: Enter ITV7 For Free EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 320,000gns yearling; third foal; Havana Grey half-brother to 6f 2yo Group 3 winner Tadej; dam placed 1m/1m2f (RPR 75), from classy family; powerful Newmarket stable is having an excellent season with 2yos; major player.

RaceName: Enter ITV7 For Free EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 170,000euros yearling who was second on debut at York in May (5f, good; 2-1 favourite) and, while he was no match for the winner, that was Cut A Dash who was subsequently fourth at Royal Ascot; the tongue-tie is retained for this first run since; entered in the Group 2 Mill Reef; sets a useful standard.

RaceName: Enter ITV7 For Free EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Second foal; St Mark's Basilica half-sister to connections 5f/6f 2yo winner Catching The Moon (including Group 3); dam 1m4f winner (RPR 72), half-sister to Group-placed 5f 2yo winner Pearls And Rubies, out of 1m2f Group 1 winner; takes on males on debut but no surprise to see a good run.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Yet to add to tally since maiden win at Tipperary last year; good third at Leopardstown in May (1m2f, good) but hasn't built on that and handicapper slow to relent.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Dual 1m winner in Britain, both on good ground; steady return to form of late, most recently in first-time visor at Galway, racing keenly when good third of 16 over 1m4f (yielding); step back in trip could suit now.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Lightly raced Ghaiyyath colt; promising debut in C&D maiden on Derby weekend and following month justified favouritism in similar Down Royal contest, still green but asserting late on to win a shade snugly; likely has more to offer and interesting stepping into handicap company.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Only win from 24 starts came on heavy ground at Gowran last September; couple of good placed efforts at Leopardstown this term but needs to improve on recent form.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Best on AW (six wins) but just 1-21 on turf; scored at Dundalk in March but soundly beaten back on turf of late; jockey booking encouraging off a reduced mark.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Nicely improved on yard debut to win over this trip at Navan last month, didn't appear to stay 1m4f at Galway 16 days later; could still have more to offer at this trip.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Sole win came in an AW 7f maiden at Dundalk in December; had the run of the race under today's rider in a premier handicap here (1m1f, good) when a career-best third but unable to back that up over shorter at Galway; tries this trip for the first time.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Won a 7f maiden (yielding) on debut at the Galway festival last season; only seen three times since, never sighted on last month's handicap debut at Leopardstown (7f); marked step up in trip here and could be a suspect stayer.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Lightly raced 3yo, easily pick of three maiden runs when rallying 1l third to Youcansaythatagain over this trip at Down Royal; well below that form at Galway since however over shorter; should appreciate return to 1m2f for handicap debut.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: AW winner at this trip last autumn and easily best of three turf runs this summer when beaten a neck over this trip at Leopardstown; may not have handled the track at Galway latest (softer ground) but definite chance on that Leopardstown run.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Nicely improved on third maiden outing this summer to land Ballinrobe contest over just shy of this trip, just outbattling a subsequent winner (pair clear); opening mark looks handy, could go well.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap
Spotlight: Has been in good form this summer with wins at both Killarney and Leopardstown over slightly shorter; decent run at Ballinrobe afterwards, but Gowran effort on Wednesday was disappointing; 3lb out of handicap here.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner won a Galway beginners' chase last year but hasn't been as good since; however, there was more encouragement at Kilbeggan last time and he drops in class today so isn't dismissed.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Maiden hurdle winner here; both chase wins came at Kilbeggan when with Henry de Bromhead; below form last four starts and needs a return to his best.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Dual chase winner was second over hurdles at Killarney in May and ran a cracker back over fences at Galway last time; looks a big player down 2lb and in grade.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Won over 3m at Limerick on return, her second chase win, but was poor at Wexford since and has to rebound; was disappointing on her only previous run here.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
OwnerName: Pat Tennyson & N P Morrissey & Raymond Micheal Cody
Spotlight: Won this race last year but has been mostly below form this year over hurdles and fences; is still 3lb above last year's winning mark so has to return to best.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Point winner has only had six runs under rules; promising Kilbeggan chasing debut but not as good twice since; however, can do better again now entering handicaps.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Dual chase winner has run well in defeat at this track; however, was pulled-up on his last chase run and below form over hurdles since so others preferred.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Hurdle winner has twice run well in defeat at this track over fences this year, including over C&D; unseated at Galway last time but has a squeak on those better earlier runs.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Three hurdle wins; dual chase winner at Thurles; ran well enough at Galway last time but needs to do more today even dropped 2lb.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Hurdle winner ran well enough on h'cap chase debut at Punchestown but was poor over hurdles last time at Ballinrobe; the cheekpieces worn then are left off today so he could rebound.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: Exposed as a limited hurdler and makes no appeal on this belated Flat debut.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: Has performed to a low level in both his races over 7f.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: 85,000gns yearling; settled in rear at Wolverhampton (7f; 25-1) and never made any great inroads up the straight; best watched for now.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: Son of Blue Point who cost 80,000gns as a yearling; half-brother to 6f winner Thelma's Angel (RPR 88); dam Listed-placed 5f/5.4f winner (109); has been gelded but needs checking out in the betting.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: 30,000gns yearling by Ardad; sixth foal; closely related to winners Yazaman (Group-placed 5f/5.5f; RPR 103) and Poderoso (Qatari 6f/7f), and half-brother to 5f-6.5f winner Royal Commando (114); dam Listed-placed 5f winner (105); gelded prior to this debut but pedigree bodes well.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: £170,000 yearling; went off at only 7-2 for last year's debut at Windsor (6f, good) but never really got involved from off the pace; gelded in the meantime and it will be interesting to gauge the confidence behind him after 11 months off.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: Clear promise in both his runs over 6f, last time beaten half a length behind one who hasn't disgraced the form since; sets the standard.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: 230,000gns breeze-up buy last year; raced with choke out and was turned over at odds of 4-7 on debut at Hamilton (5f, good) that May; second run has been a long time coming and he's now gelded; market vibes are awaited with interest.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: First foal out of a 7f-8.6f AW winner (RPR 98) and half-sister to winners Revenite (6f 2yo) and Global Art (1m-1m2f); tongue tied for debut; she'd be a surprise winner unless the money comes.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
Spotlight: Out the back in races at Windsor and Bath; handicaps beckon; stablemate of form choice Space Party.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Front-runner who posted five wins last year and reappeared with another at Musselburgh (1m, good) in April; unplaced on both starts since and, while she didn't run badly back at Musselburgh last time, she's taking on 3yos this afternoon and may again prove vulnerable.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: 1m AW novice winner who was beaten just over 3l when eighth of 14 on last month's handicap debut at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good); that came after a break and she may be able to build on that performance today; a possible.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won Leicester maiden (6f, good to firm) in May on third start and progressive in handicaps since, going close behind Darzah at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) then making all at Nottingham (1m, good to firm); came clear with the runner-up last time and she's very much respected up 6lb.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Beat Luna Celeste to win at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) in June on her second handicap start; disappointing behind that rival at Nottingham (1m, good to firm) subsequently but she retains potential for her top yard; could be on a good mark if bouncing back to form.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: She's run to a similar level on all five starts and made all in a five-runner maiden at Nottingham (1m, good to firm) a fortnight ago; improvement is needed if she's to follow up on this handicap debut but she's unexposed in the hood (worn on last two starts) and is not ruled out.

RaceName: Newbridge Silverware Royal Whip Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Handicap winner over 1m4f at Goodwood last season; low-key efforts in April/May before showing signs of a return to form when fifth in a 1m4f Royal Ascot handicap; faded into fourth behind Ethical Diamond in a 1m4f Group 3 event at Leopardstown ten days ago.

RaceName: Newbridge Silverware Royal Whip Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Holds outstanding claims here despite having only a debut win to his name; form last season and this term ties in with several top-class Ballydoyle colts, including when fourth behind three of them in the Prix du Jockey-Club and when splitting Constitution River and Hawk Mountain in the Eclipse.

RaceName: Newbridge Silverware Royal Whip Stakes (Group 3)
OwnerName: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith
Spotlight: Useful form in juvenile maidens, culminating in a 6f Cork win on yielding-to-soft last September; found to be lame when an unplaced favourite for a 6f Listed race at Fairyhouse later that month; makes a belated return; may outrun his 89 rating but faces a huge task

RaceName: Newbridge Silverware Royal Whip Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Debut maiden winner on soft at Gowran in April, saw out the extended 1m1f well despite running green; moderate fourth of five at Roscommon the following month; cheekpieces fitted now; up against it.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Six-time winner, including over C&D in a novice chase two years ago; form has been in and out over the last 12 months but best effort in that time came over C&D when 4.25l second off 4lb higher in May; below form last twice, pulled up at Wexford 47 days ago; on a good mark if return to this track sparks him up again.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Maiden hurdle winner last year who bounced back to form with second at Wexford (2m1f, good) in May; backed that up when beaten 6l into fifth at Listowel when out of the weights; below form when beaten favourite at Wexford lto; makes chase debut and appeals as the type with more to give.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Veteran who is 12-115 under all codes; five-time course winner, four times over jumps; dual C&D winner, latest 12 months ago off 7lb higher; much below best last two vists here but dangerous to completely write off in a winnable race at a venue he loves.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Three-time winner over hurdles, latest in October 2024; last two hurdle runs have been poor and was well-held 2lb higher in handicap chase at Roscommon in June; needs plenty more in first-time hood.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: 250-1 maiden hurdle winner two years ago; couple of decent runs in handicaps last year but form largely inconsistent; beaten 15l into fourth at Killarney (2m1f, good) 31 days ago over hurdles, staying on reasonably well from rear; beaten 21l over C&D in May; on a nice mark but needs to put best foot forward.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: A 15-race maiden but her best form has come here; beaten 3.5l into third by well-handicapped rival over C&D in October off 7lb higher; below form three starts this term but she would have a big chance if reproducing October effort.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: AW winner in Britain; hasn't shown anything of note in six hurdle starts; needs far more on chase debut

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Has been struggling in handicaps but ran one of his better races 13 days ago when keeping on to finish fifth at Cork (2m1f, good); needs fences to spark improvement.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: A 14-race maiden but has had some good efforts, most notably when second at Punchestown (3m, good) in May off 4lb higher; well-held in four starts since and tries a shorter trip over fences; capable off this mark.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: First foal out of a 5f/6f winner for this yard, including on the Newcastle AW; however, this is a belated debut and he's probably up against it.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Both runs over 5f; his third last time came in a field of four and he was beaten just over 8l, as was also the case on his debut.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Son of Frankel but never raced for Godolphin after making 500,000gns as a yearling and was sold on this February for 16,000gns (gelded before then); a watching brief makes sense.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: 40,000gns yearling and a half-brother to four winners; made his debut over 7f on Tapeta at Wolverhampton (14-1) where he didn't enjoy the clearest of runs before keeping on, finishing 7l off the winner; the runner-up has given that form a hefty boost; should be wiser here and get involved, for all that dropping back to 6f may ask different questions of him.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Went from the front when beaten 2l at Newcastle and had a wide draw when not so good at Wolverhampton (again over 5f; did some hanging); others in here have superior form but he'll win races further down the line, if not this one.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Beaten in the region of 15l in 6f races at Lingfield and Wolverhampton; one for handicaps.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: 160,000gns yearling; weak 10-1 at Leicester (7f) but saw his race out well for second of four after starting slowly, and the winner had shown plenty of promise previously; this drop back to 6f wouldn't be an obvious move but he's a scopey gelding with better days ahead of him.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: Well-bred filly who has finished second in both her races, beaten 7l on debut but then just over 2l at Wetherby (extended 5f) where she got no freedom up front; take out the winner and that was a weak race, but she retains potential.

RaceName: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
Spotlight: 72,000gns yearling and a half-sister to four winners; also hooded at Lingfield in May (extended 7f, good) and ran with a degree of promise behind respected opposition; needs to find more but that's feasible, especially back at 6f as she travelled okay on that debut.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: This is her first run since last July but she returns with her stable in fine form and she went very close in the Group 2 Sandy Lane Stakes at Haydock (6f, good) last May; in the mix if at the top of her game; wears a first-time tongue-tie.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Raced wide when well beaten at 150-1 in Group 3 Oak Tree Stakes at Goodwood (7f, good to firm) recently; unplaced in three Listed races prior to that; hard to fancy.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Down the field in Group 3 Oak Tree Stakes at Goodwood (7f, good to firm) last time but prior to that she went close in two Listed races at Chester (7f, good); has a part to play if leaving last time behind.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: 0-13 since winning on her debut in August 2024 but she was second in this last year (good to firm) and has been running well in defeat in Listed races this season; there's every chance that she'll be thereabouts.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: 0-5, all in Group races, since winning on debut last July but she's produced some big performances in the interim, most recently a close fourth in the Group 3 Summer Stakes at York (6f, good to firm); that latest form has worked out well and this front-runner can make a bold bid from stall two.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Made it 2-3 in 2yo campaign with Group 3 win at Ayr last September; she's had excuses on both runs this season (interference; upset in stalls) but has been well beaten each time and others arrive with less to prove.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Exploited a reduced mark to win Class 4 handicap at Ascot (5f, good to firm) last month; this 3yo may have more to offer now that things have clicked again but she looks up against it in today's line-up.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
OwnerName: E S-O Racing Club And Elaine Chivers
Spotlight: 3yo who made her debut only in May; made all at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in June on her third start then did likewise on handicap debut at Leicester (6f, good to firm); others have more substance to their form but she was impressive last time and it remains to be seen where her limitations lie.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Won the Group 2 Lowther Stakes at York (6f, good to firm) last August and she took a step back in the right direction when 3l fifth of 13 there last month in the Group 3 Summer Stakes (6f, good to firm; America Queen fourth), when slowly away in first-time tongue-tie/cheekpieces (both retained); she's capable of building on that latest effort and is one to consider.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Won handicap at Chester (6f, good) in May and ran well when fifth of 20 in competitive fillies' handicap at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good) last time; however, she has plenty to find against the pick of today's opposition.

RaceName: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Lightly raced 3yo who was sold out of William Haggas's yard for 6,000gns on July 1 and has proved to be a bargain buy for new connections, making it 2-2 for current yard when winning big-field fillies' handicap at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good); today's assignment demands further improvement but she's clearly thriving and is not ruled out.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Well beaten on debut when trained by Archie Watson but 2-2 since joining this yard, showing plenty of speed when up with the pace in winning Bellewstown maiden and Cork rated event (much better form) on good-to-firm; should make another bold bid although stiffer 5f here.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: C&D debut winner in April (soft) is 0-4 since, notably Cork rated third to Grayrobin (rec 5lb); never able to land a blow in valuable Ballyhane Stakes on first run over 6f latest; place claims.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Promising Naas debut in June was quickly followed by a Bellewstown maiden win at this trip (good); unable to handle step up to Listed company on latest and needs to find more.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: Team Valor International, D Dias,M Eves
Spotlight: All three runs have been in Britain, winning Goodwood novice in May, beaten a head in York Listed a fortnight later and creditable ninth of 27 behind Victorious in Group 2 Queen Mary at Ascot on good-to-firm; has had a break since and heads a strong stable challenge here.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Maiden whose standout run came when fifth of 10 in Naas Listed last month, fourth in Cork maiden on Friday.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Plenty of experience, winning Naas maiden (beating April Mist 2.5l) and much better form when narrowly defeated in Listed at same venue last month; keen when beaten 5l in Group 3 Molecomb Stakes on latest; definite claims.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Sioux Nation filly made favourable first impression with a 5l Naas maiden win last month but ran below expectations (favourite) in Fillies' Listed over same C&D 18 days later, keen to post and not quite getting home when fourth to a stablemate; tried hooded now and remains capable of better.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Second runner for the owners/trainer; 0-3 in 6f maidens, including Naas third to a subsequent Group 2 winner, and didn't quite get home here a week ago; back in trip now and don't rule out.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Yet to trouble the judge in four runs; looks out of her depth here.

RaceName: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Space Traveller half-sister to Polish 6f 2yo winner Serce; dam Listed-placed 5f winner (RPR 92), half-sister to winners Brooklands Bay (8.6f 2yo) and Majestic Timeline (5f); likely outsider of the yard's trio of runners, all the better for the experience.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: 3,000euros foal by Blue Bresil; dam unraced half-sister to winners Croco Bay (smart 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase) and Thistle Do Nicely (useful bumper and 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase); yard had bumper winner here in May.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Slipped up when struggling on debut at Thurles; off 239 days; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Dam unraced half-sister to 2m chase winner Majorica King and French 1m7f hurdle/2m1f chase winner Six Fois Sept, out of Listed-placed 1m2f winner; market can dictate expectations on debut.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Stepped forward with each of her three stars for Adrian Murray; 8l second to subsequent winner at Clonmel (2m4f, yielding) 124 days ago having raced with enthusiasm in the lead in first-time hood; looks solid form and drop in trip should help on stable debut; hood left off; leading player.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Didn't show a great deal in first three runs but much improved when beaten 4.5l into sixth at Sligo (extended 2m2f, good) 10 days ago; could be flattered by that however and needs to build on it.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Showed ability on debut when beaten 16l in good Galway bumper a year ago; backwards step when returned from long absence at Killarney 31 days ago, beaten 21l; market expected better; should come on for that and not to be dismissed based on debut.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Half-sister to some smart performers; showed ability when making late headway to be beaten 11.5l into fifth on debut at Killarney 31 days ago; hails from top yard; improvement expected and should be thereabouts.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Elusive Pimpernel mare; half-sister to point winner Break The Boundary; dam point winner, half-sister to 5f 2yo winner Cloudea; not an obvious type on paper to make a winning debut.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: A 1,400 euros foal; dam unraced half-sister to 3m hurdle/chase winner Lunar Contact, out of unraced sister to Champion Bumper and smart 2m2f-2m4f hurdle/chase winner Briar Hill; decent pedigree and market can guide on debut.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: A 12,000euros foal; half-sister to Czech 6f 2yo winner Dantawi; unraced dam closely related to useful 7f/1m winner Akira, half-sister to 1m1f Flat/2m hurdle winner Halling Gal, out of unraced half-sister to 1m2f Group 3 winner Husyan; bred to be sharp; yard gets bumper winners.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Decent fourth over C&D on debut but followed up with poor effort at Cork; more like it last time when beaten 15.5l into seventh at Galway (extended 2m, good) keeping on; each-way shout.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Didn't complete in two point-to-points but outran odds when third past the post (demoted to fourth) at Galway 14 days ago; she was probably flattered by proximity but the first two are potentially smart so it was a positive effort; good chance here in winnable race.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: New trainer decides against the cheekpieces (and regular tongue-tie) that worked well for this 4yo in his last two races, when he had the outside stall at Kempton and raced wide throughout at Wolverhampton (again over 6f); C&D winner with a good chance.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Three-time winner but 0-13 since moving yards and doesn't look about to put that right.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Best form was as a 2yo when twice successful; falling in the weights but this season hasn't got up and running.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Made all at Nottingham (5f, soft) and bang there on starts either side of that, beaten under a length; solid chance with C&D form to his name.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Won off 3lb higher over 6f on the AW for previous yard; unplaced so far for current one, offering little in last two races.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: No wins in nine; has gone close in 6f/7f handicaps (one on Polytrack) but prone to off days, as he reminded us last time at Yarmouth.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: All three wins have been here but over 7f and for different yards; however, close up on stable debut over 6f at Ripon and last run wasn't too bad as he was never in the right place at Lingfield; don't put a line through him.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Only 1-26 but that win was three runs back over 7f at Wolverhampton and it had been coming; has continued to run well and 6f is fine, as is this track.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Regressive maiden who continues to race freely, so dropping back from 7f might be no bad thing; wouldn't be the percentage play, though.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Has won on turf but better on the AW and gave it a good go under a front-running ride last month at Wolverhampton (7f; just behind On Key); better known for his exploits at this trip; an exposed 9yo but not without hope.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Sole win was in 2023 but she's lightly raced for a 6yo; ran on late over 5f here two months ago when making AW debut after nearly a year off; if sharper for that, and returning to her winning trip, she should go well.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: No wins in 14 but twice runner-up this year over 6f and tried 7f last time, running another fair race; could drop lucky one day.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Left the Faheys for 3,500gns as an eight-race maiden; needs to halt the slide in his form.

RaceName: GB Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Inconsistency has crept in but she ran really well from a bad draw at Pontefract last time (6f) and has won here before.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 0-7 in handicaps and expensive to follow but he's run some big races this season, most recently second of six at Newmarket (1m2f, good to firm) behind a well-handicapped winner; wears first-time cheekpieces and can be bang there off the same mark as last time.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up off 1lb higher at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) in April and he's run respectably on his three starts since; this is less competitive than those last three outings and he might not be far away.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
